citation: Zhang X, Zhang L, Li Y, Wang N, Zhang Y. Clinical performance of metagenomic next-generation sequencing for diagnosis of invasive fungal disease after hematopoietic cell transplant. Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology. 2024;14:1210857.

population.n_total: 189 screened/at risk for IFD; 46 IFD patients analyzed
population.population_description: HSCT recipients at risk of IFD (prolonged FN after >=96 h broad-spectrum antibiotics, FN recurrence, or other suspicion of fungal infection), Tongji Hospital, Huazhong University of Science and Technology; Table 1 reports n=46 with IFD

neutropenic_status: Enrollment criterion: prolonged fever with neutropenia after broad-spectrum antibiotics (>=96 h), or FN recurrence (febrile neutropenia per standard definition); 25/46 (54.35%) agranulocytic

specimens.n_tests: 3 mL blood collected; 300 uL plasma extracted (main specimen)

index_test.platform_or_panel: mNGS, DNase-free DNA library, sequenced on MGISEQ-200/MGISEQ-2000 (DNB nanoball); DNA only
index_test.commercial_or_inhouse: in-house (BGI-style pipeline; positivity criteria defined with RPM/NTC ratios)

reference_standard: EORTC/MSGERC revised definitions plus Chinese guidelines: proven/probable/possible/undefined IFD classification (1 proven, 11 probable, 27 possible, 7 undefined among 46)

comparator_2x2.against: conventional microbiological testing (CMT) among the 46 IFD patients (Table 2)
comparator_2x2.note: Table printed vs CMT, not vs EORTC final classification; XML table totals garbled ('Total 9 7 46' likely 39/7/46; row 'Negative 24 5 28' sums to 29, not 28). Verify against PDF before pooling. Detectability: mNGS 84.78% vs CMT 36.96% of 46 patients.

diagnostic_yield.n_positive_relevant_pathogens: mNGS positive in 39/46 (84.78%); CMT positive 17/46 (36.96%); 15 concordant positive
diagnostic_yield.basis: detectability of fungal pathogens among 46 IFD patients

additional_yield_vs_conventional: mNGS detected fungi in 24 patients who were CMT-negative; CMT-positive/mNGS-negative in 2 patients (one Candida albicans bloodstream infection missed by mNGS); 15 patients concordant.
turnaround_time: "The detection time was significantly reduced using mNGS" - numeric TAT not extractable from text
therapy_change: Antifungal therapy regimens reported per pathogen group (Table 3); 35/46 (76.09%) on prophylactic therapy; no explicit mNGS-driven therapy-change counts
mortality_or_outcomes: The fungi-related mortality rate was 18.82% (95% CI, 9.08%-30.72%); median time from fungal infection to death or end of follow-up was 11.79 months (Table 3: improved/death counts per group).

quality_flags.overlap_risk: Single center; only 46 of 189 at-risk patients analyzed (IFD cases); mNGS part of EORTC-compatible work-up

quadas2_notes: Retrospective; reference standard is EORTC classification (microbiology/GM/CT/imaging) but the numeric mNGS-vs-EORTC 2x2 is not given in text - Table 2 is mNGS vs CMT with garbled XML totals. Possible incorporation bias as mNGS could inform classification. No numeric TAT.

evidence_quotes.quote: We retrospectively studied 189 patients who underwent HSCT and were considered at risk of IFD at the Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation Center, Tongji Hospital, affiliated with Huazhong University of Science and Technology, between June 2020 and October 2022.
In total, 46 patients were diagnosed with IFD, and the prevalence of proven, probable, possible, and undefined IFD was 2.18% (1), 23.91% (11), 58.69% (27), and 15.22% (7), respectively.
Table 2 Performance of mNGS and CMT in all patients with IFD. mNGS CMT Positive Negative Total Positive 15 2 17 Negative 24 5 28 Total 9 7 46
The detectability increased significantly from 36.96% to 84.78%.
The mNGS results for 15 patients were consistent with those of CMT.
In two incidents the CMT results in this study were positive, but the NGS produced a false negative in two patients.

At least one of the following enrollment criteria was present: (1) prolonged fever with neutropenia (FN) after broad-spectrum antibiotics (≥ 96 h), (2) FN recurrence, or (3) anomalous conditions to consider fungal infections.
The fungi-related mortality rate was 18.82% (95% CI, 9.08%–30.72%).
Quality-qualified libraries were pooled, and DNA Nanoball (DNB) was made and sequenced by MGISEQ-200/MGISEQ-2000 platform
